description: Change of use of the first, second, and third floors from Office (Class E) to five flats (Class C3) (2 x 2 bed, 1 x 1 bed, and 2 x Studio); external alterations
decision_conditions: <p><span style="font-size: 14px;">The proposed residential units, by reason of their unsatisfactory internal layout, the absence of sufficient information regarding floor-to-ceiling heights, and the lack of adequate information to assess potential environmental health impacts from surrounding uses, have failed to demonstrate that a satisfactory standard of accommodation would be provided for future occupiers. Taken cumulatively, these deficiencies would result in a poor quality living environment, contrary to Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy GR1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041), the Residential Design Guide SPD (2010), and the Mayor's Housing SPG (2023).</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 14px;">The proposed change of use of the first, second and third floors from Office (Class E) to residential use (Class C3) would result in the unjustified loss of office accommodation within Harrow’s Metropolitan Town Centre, a location identified as a primary focus for commercial and employment generating uses. In the absence of satisfactory evidence demonstrating that the premises have been actively marketed for a minimum period of 24 months and are no longer required for office or other appropriate town centre uses, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the loss of the commercial floorspace is acceptable. The proposal would therefore undermine the role and function of the Metropolitan Town Centre and is contrary to Policies SP05C and LE1, together with Appendix 6, of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 14px;">The proposed development fails to demonstrate satisfactory vertical stacking of habitable rooms, resulting in an unacceptable relationship between internal uses across floors. In particular, habitable rooms would be positioned above and/or below non-habitable spaces, increasing the potential for noise and disturbance between units and resulting in a poor standard of residential accommodation for future occupiers. As such, the proposal would fail to provide a high quality living environment and would be contrary to Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy GR1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041), the Residential Design Guide SPD (2010) and the Mayor's Housing SPG (2023).&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 14px;">The proposed development, by reason of its housing mix comprising two studio flats, one one-bedroom flat and two two-bedroom flats, would fail to provide a housing mix that adequately responds to identified local housing needs, particularly in respect of family-sized accommodation. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy H10 the London Plan (2021) and Policy HO1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041) which seek to secure an appropriate and balanced mix of dwelling sizes across the borough.&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 14px;">The applicant has failed to demonstrate that adequate refuse and recycling facilities would be provided for the development. In particular, no clear distinction has been made between the storage areas serving the ground floor commercial unit and the proposed residential accommodation. As a result, it has not been demonstrated that waste and recycling arising from the different uses can be appropriately segregated and managed. The proposal would therefore result in inadequate waste storage arrangements, to the detriment of the functionality of the development and the amenities of future occupiers, contrary to Policies D4 and SI 8 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy CE1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021 – 2041) and Harrow’s Code of Practice for Storage and Collection of Refuse and Materials for Recycling in Domestic Properties (2023).&nbsp;</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal">The proposed development, in the absence of a
Legal Agreement to restrict parking permits to future occupiers would fail to adequately
mitigate the impact on parking capacity arising from the development on the
immediate and wider area, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework
(2026), policies T6 of The London Plan (2021) and Policies M1 and M2 of the
Harrow Local Plan (2021 – 2041).<o:p></o:p></p>
